examples.en: We call our country the land of beautiful rivers and mountains stretching three thousand ri.

examples.ko: 가을 설악산은 정말 금수강산 그 자체예요.
examples.en: Seoraksan in autumn is truly a land of beautiful scenery itself.
To protect our beautiful land, we have to take care of the environment first.

examples.ko: 경치가 좋은 곳에 가면 할아버지는 '금수강산이 따로 없네'라고 하세요.
examples.en: When we go somewhere with a nice view, my grandfather says, 'This is as beautiful as it gets.'

examples.ko: 아름다운 금수강산에 쓰레기를 버리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not throw trash on our beautiful land.
This song sings about the four seasons of our beautiful land.

explain: 비단에 수를 놓은 것처럼 아름다운 산과 강이라는 말이고, 특히 우리나라를 가리킬 때 많이 써요. '삼천리 금수강산'이라는 표현으로 자주 나오고, 경치에 감탄할 때 '금수강산이 따로 없다'고도 말해요.

phrases.en: I am proud of our beautiful land of three thousand ri.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우리나라를 가리킬 때 가장 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common expression when referring to Korea.

phrases.example: 단풍이 든 산을 보니 금수강산이 따로 없네요.
phrases.en: Seeing the mountain in autumn colors, it's truly a land of beauty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경치가 너무 아름다워서 감탄할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said in admiration when the scenery is wonderfully beautiful.

phrases.en: This valley is the very picture of beautiful scenery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곳이 아름다운 산과 강의 모습 그대로라고 감탄할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in admiration when a place is the perfect picture of beautiful mountains and rivers.
phrases.en_equiv: the very picture of beautiful scenery

explain_en: It means mountains and rivers as beautiful as silk embroidery, and is used especially to refer to Korea. It often appears in the phrase '삼천리 금수강산', and people also say '금수강산이 따로 없다' when admiring a view.

examples.ko: 강 주변의 땅은 비옥해서 농사짓기 좋아요.
examples.en: The land around the river is fertile, so it's good for farming.
I heard the rice is delicious because it grew in fertile soil.
If you add fertilizer, the soil becomes more fertile.

examples.ko: 비옥하지 않은 땅에서도 자라는 식물이 있어요.
examples.en: Some plants grow even in soil that isn't fertile.
Farmers work hard to keep their soil fertile.
Plains are known to be fertile.

explain: 우리말로는 땅이 '기름지다'라고도 하는데, '비옥하다'는 조금 더 딱딱한 말이라 글이나 설명에서 잘 어울려요. 땅·토지·토양에 쓰고, 반대말은 '척박하다'예요.

phrases.en: Vegetables grow well in fertile soil.
phrases.nuance_ko: '땅' 대신 '토양'을 쓰면 설명하는 글에 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using 'soil' instead of 'land' fits explanatory writing better.

phrases.en: If you add fertilizer, the land becomes fertile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅이 좋아지는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes land changing to become fertile.

phrases.example: 이 마을은 기름진 땅 덕분에 농사가 잘돼요.
phrases.en: Farming goes well in this village thanks to its rich land.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비옥한 땅'과 뜻은 같고, 말할 때 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'fertile land' but more conversational.

explain_en: Koreans also say a field is '기름지다', but '비옥하다' is a bit more formal and fits writing and explanations. It is used for land, soil and earth, and its opposite is '척박하다' (barren).

examples.ko: 물을 못 줘서 화초가 시들시들 말라 가요.
examples.en: I couldn't water them, so the plants are drying up and wilting.
The flowers look limp and weak.
The vegetables I left out for a few days have gone limp.

examples.ko: 더위에 지친 강아지가 시들시들 누워 있어요.
examples.en: The puppy, worn out by the heat, is lying there listlessly.

examples.ko: 화분 속 풀이 시들시들 고개를 숙였어요.
examples.en: The plant in the pot has drooped its head.

examples.ko: 열이 나서 아이가 시들시들 기운이 없어요.
examples.en: The child has a fever and is droopy and weak.

explain: 식물이 말라서 힘없이 늘어진 모양을 말해요. 사람이나 동물이 기운이 없는 모습에도 비유로 써요. 병으로 오래 앓는 모습을 말하는 '시름시름'과 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: The leaves drooped limply in the heat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물이 힘없이 아래로 늘어지는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a plant sagging down without strength.

phrases.en: If you don't water them, the flowers wilt.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-해지다'를 붙여 점점 변하는 과정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -해지다 describes the gradual process of change.

phrases.en: The flowers wilted in just a few days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기본 동사로, 식물이 마르고 생기를 잃을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The base verb, for a plant drying out and losing its life.

explain_en: It describes a plant drying out and drooping without strength. It is also used figuratively for people or animals lacking energy. Don't confuse it with '시름시름', which describes being ill for a long time.

en: to be dusky; to be dim

examples.en: The sky is dim now that the sun has set.
The room was dim, so I turned on the light.
I walked alone down the dimly lit alley.
The faint light of dawn came in through the window.
We played outside until it got dusky.
The mountain looked beautiful, faintly visible in the dim light.

explain: 완전히 깜깜하지 않고 빛이 희미하게 남은 상태에 써요. '어스름한 골목', '날이 어스름해지다'처럼 쓰고, 명사 '어스름'과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: I saw a cat in the dim alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빛이 희미하게 남은 장소를 꾸며 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a place where only faint light remains.

phrases.en: I go home when it gets dim.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점점 어두워지는 변화를 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the gradual change as it gets darker.

phrases.en: I got up in the dim early dawn and exercised.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해가 뜨기 전 빛이 희미한 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the faintly lit time just before sunrise.

explain_en: It describes a state that is not completely dark, with faint light remaining. It is used as in '어스름한 골목' or '날이 어스름해지다', and it is good to learn it together with the noun '어스름'.

examples.en: In summer it's good to rest in the shade.
The snow in the shady spots hasn't melted yet.

examples.ko: 빨래를 응달에 널면 잘 안 말라요.
examples.en: If you hang laundry in the shade, it doesn't dry well.

examples.ko: 이 화분은 응달도 괜찮아서 키우기 쉬워요.
examples.en: This plant is fine even in the shade, so it's easy to grow.
It's a shady spot, so it's a bit cold even in the daytime.

examples.ko: 우리 집 뒤쪽은 응달이라 겨울에 얼음이 많아요.
examples.en: The back of our house is in shadow, so there is a lot of ice in winter.

explain: '그늘'은 나무나 건물 때문에 생긴 어두운 자리이고, '응달'은 방향 때문에 해가 잘 들지 않는 곳이에요. 반대말은 햇볕이 잘 드는 '양달'이에요. 한자어로는 '음지'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: It was hot, so I rested in the shade for a bit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '-에서'를 붙여 해가 잘 안 드는 곳에서 하는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-에서' it tells what you do in a place that gets little sun.

phrases.example: 산에는 응달과 양달의 기온 차이가 커요.
phrases.en: On a mountain, the temperature difference between shade and sunny spots is big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말인 '양달'과 함께 쓰면 두 곳을 비교하기 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with its opposite '양달', it makes comparing two spots easy.

phrases.example: 응달 쪽 방은 겨울에 많이 추워요.
phrases.en: A room on the shady side is very cold in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해가 잘 안 드는 방향의 집이나 방을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a house or room facing away from the sun.
phrases.en_equiv: a room on the shady side

explain_en: '그늘' is a dark spot made by a tree or a building, while '응달' is a place that gets little sun because of the direction it faces. The opposite is '양달', a sunny spot. The Sino-Korean word '음지' means the same.

en: to be steadfast; to be unwavering

examples.en: The rain is pouring down relentlessly again.

examples.ko: 그는 십 년 동안 줄기차게 같은 주장을 했어요.
examples.en: He kept making the same argument for ten years.
After tireless effort, I finally passed.
The opposition was so persistent that the meeting ran long.
The summer rainy season is relentless and lasts long.

examples.ko: 그 팀의 응원은 경기 내내 줄기찼어요.
examples.en: That team's cheering never let up throughout the game.

explain: 비, 노력, 주장처럼 오랫동안 끊이지 않고 계속되는 것에 써요. 주로 '줄기차게 내리다/주장하다'처럼 부사형으로 많이 나와요. '꾸준하다'보다 기세가 세고 끈질기다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: The rain kept pouring all night long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비나 눈이 그치지 않고 계속 내리는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for rain or snow that keeps falling without stopping.

phrases.example: 그는 십 년 동안 줄기차게 같은 의견을 주장했어요.
phrases.en: He has insisted on the same opinion for ten years without letting up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 생각을 굽히지 않고 계속 말하는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows someone repeating their view without giving in.

phrases.en: The students persistently demanded better facilities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끈질기게 계속 요구하는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows someone demanding something stubbornly and continuously.

explain_en: It is used for things that go on for a long time without stopping, such as rain, effort or an argument. It most often appears as an adverb, like '줄기차게 내리다' or '줄기차게 주장하다'. Compared with '꾸준하다', it feels stronger and more persistent.

examples.en: This water passed the heavy metal test.
Lead and mercury are typical heavy metals.

examples.ko: 중금속은 한번 몸에 쌓이면 잘 빠지지 않아요.
examples.en: Once heavy metals build up in the body, they don't leave easily.

examples.ko: 공장 근처 땅에서 중금속이 나왔다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that heavy metals were found in the soil near the factory.
I bought a water purifier that filters out heavy metals.

examples.ko: 중금속에 오염된 흙은 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: Soil polluted with heavy metals cannot be used.

explain: 납, 수은, 카드뮴처럼 무거운 금속을 말하고, 환경이나 건강 뉴스에서 '중금속 오염', '중금속 검사'로 자주 나와요. 보통 몸에 나쁘다는 뜻과 함께 쓰여요. 일상 대화보다는 설명하거나 보도하는 말에 가까워요.

phrases.en: Heavy metal pollution in the river is serious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경 뉴스에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in environmental news.

phrases.en: Heavy metal poisoning is very dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중금속이 몸에 쌓여 병이 되는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to illness caused by heavy metals building up in the body.

phrases.example: 이 생선에는 중금속이 조금 들어 있어요.
phrases.en: This fish contains a little heavy metal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 물에 중금속이 있는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say whether food or water contains heavy metals.

explain_en: It refers to heavy metals like lead, mercury and cadmium, and often appears in environmental and health news as '중금속 오염' or '중금속 검사'. It is usually used in the sense of being harmful to the body. It sounds closer to explanations and news reports than casual conversation.

en: to be barren; to be infertile

examples.ko: 이 땅은 너무 척박해서 농사짓기 어려워요.
examples.en: This land is too barren, so it's hard to farm.

examples.ko: 산 위쪽 땅은 척박하지만 이 나무는 잘 자라요.
examples.en: The land higher up the mountain is poor, but this tree grows well.
Deserts lack water, so the soil is barren.

examples.ko: 예전에는 척박했던 이곳이 지금은 푸른 숲이에요.
examples.en: This place used to be barren, but now it's a green forest.

examples.ko: 문화 환경이 척박한 시골에서 도서관을 열었어요.
examples.en: I opened a library in a countryside area with a poor cultural environment.
It's a piece of land that looks barren because of all the stones.

explain: 땅이 메말라서 식물이 자라기 힘든 상태를 말해요. 반대로 땅이 좋을 때는 '기름지다', '비옥하다'라고 해요. 사람이 살거나 일하는 환경이 힘들 때도 '척박한 환경', '척박한 현실'처럼 비유로 써요.

phrases.en: Some grasses grow even in barren land.
phrases.nuance_ko: 활용형으로 명사 '땅'을 꾸밀 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use: modifying the noun 땅 (land).

phrases.en: The soil here is barren.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 쓰는 해요체로, 상태를 간단히 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite spoken form, used to simply describe a condition.

phrases.en: He did not give up even in a harsh environment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅뿐 아니라 살기 힘든 상황을 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for any hard living or working conditions.

explain_en: It describes land so dry and poor that plants have a hard time growing. Good land is described as '기름지다' or '비옥하다'. It is also used figuratively when the environment for living or working is hard, as in '척박한 환경' or '척박한 현실'.

examples.en: The plane began to descend slowly.
My ears felt blocked while the elevator was going down.
The temperature dropped suddenly, so I took out my coat.
As the hot air balloon descended, the village looked bigger.
The bird swooped down fast from the sky.
The submarine will descend to the bottom of the sea.

explain: 비행기, 엘리베이터, 열기구처럼 위에서 아래로 움직이는 것에 써요. 반대말은 '상승하다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 '내려가다'를, 값이나 온도가 낮아질 때는 '떨어지다'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The hot air balloon descends slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서서히'와 함께 천천히 내려가는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '서서히', it describes a slow descent.

phrases.en: The plane is descending now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 내려가고 있는 상태를 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short way to say something is going down right now.

phrases.en: The elevator's descent speed is fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내려가는 빠르기를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for how fast something goes down.

explain_en: Use it for things moving from above to below, such as planes, elevators and hot air balloons. The opposite is 상승하다. In everyday speech Koreans say 내려가다, and for prices or temperatures, 떨어지다 is more common.

dis.h: formal: move downward, opposite of rising

p.n: Same meaning here; 하강하다 is the more general word for moving downward.

en: to be harsh; to be severe; to be bitter

examples.en: This winter's cold is much harsher than last year's.

examples.ko: 혹독한 훈련을 견디고 국가 대표가 됐어요.
examples.en: He endured brutal training and became a national team member.
Critics reviewed the new movie harshly.
The harsh winter has passed and spring has come.
The work was so grueling that I wanted to quit.
The weather isn't harsh, so it's nice for a walk.

explain: '심하다'와 비슷하지만 '혹독하다'는 추위, 훈련, 비판, 시련처럼 견디기 힘든 대상에 써서 더 무겁고 강한 느낌이에요. 날씨뿐 아니라 '혹독한 평가'처럼 사람의 태도에도 써요. '혹독한 시련을 겪다'처럼 함께 쓰는 말도 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: That movie received harsh criticism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 평가나 태도가 아주 엄하고 심할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an evaluation or attitude is very strict and severe.

phrases.en: The players trained brutally hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로 동사를 꾸며서 아주 힘들게 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form modifies a verb, meaning done in a very tough way.

phrases.en: The severe cold has continued for a week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨가 견디기 힘들 만큼 심할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the weather is hard to endure.

explain_en: It is similar to '심하다', but '혹독하다' is used for things that are hard to endure, such as cold, training, criticism and hardship, and sounds heavier and stronger. It applies not only to weather but also to attitudes, as in '혹독한 평가'. Also note collocations such as '혹독한 시련을 겪다'.
